items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And I remember Gary Keys. Do you know Gary Keys?

ctx.x: No-one defines any number of other brilliant people in whatever their field by whatever their personal proclivity is. That doesn’t get to define them.

It’s just a way to frighten you away from people in the music. That’s what it was. It was – that’s really the – we don’t know what it is. I have an old friend I went to school with in Tucson, Arizona. I went there. It’s a very white community, country clubs, just completely homogenous [?] community. I brought her a record by Cleo Laine, singing – what was his name? – Charles Ives. Cleo Laine singing Charles Ives, which is pretty traditional, standard stuff. That was Walt Whitman. The words were Walt Whitman. The…
